definitions.explanation: Extra space, time, or capacity beyond what is strictly needed.
A relaxed, unhurried state of mind. The psychological sense of having enough breathing room.

examples.japanese: {時間|じかん}にゆとりがある。
{予算|よさん}にゆとりがない。
examples.english: There's no room in the budget.

examples.japanese: ゆとりを{持|も}ってスケジュールを{組|く}んだほうがいい。
examples.english: It's better to build some margin into the schedule.

examples.japanese: {心|こころ}のゆとりが{大切|たいせつ}だ。
{忙|いそが}しくてゆとりがない。
examples.english: I'm so busy that I have no composure.

examples.japanese: ゆとりのある{生活|せいかつ}を{送|おく}りたい。
examples.english: I want to live a relaxed life.

notes:
COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {時間|じかん}のゆとり (time to spare)
- {心|こころ}のゆとり (peace of mind)
- {経済的|けいざいてき}なゆとり (financial margin)
- ゆとりを{持|も}つ (to have margin/composure)
- ゆとりがない (to have no room/composure)

CULTURAL NOTE:
ゆとり{教育|きょういく} (relaxed education) was Japan's educational reform policy from roughly 2002-2012 that reduced curriculum content and school hours. The term ゆとり{世代|せだい} (the "relaxed generation") refers to people educated under this system, sometimes used pejoratively.
